objective: As a mastery check, learners design an ongoing document-organization system for their fictional persona's entire independent-living setup - naming document categories, deciding where each category physically or digitally 'lives,' and building in a recurring monthly review habit - rather than organizing a single event's paperwork into one folder.
scenario: Unlike sorting the paperwork for one appointment or one trip into a single folder, this task asks the learner to design a standing system the persona would keep running for as long as they live independently: a small set of ongoing document categories (such as housing, income and budget, health, and identification), a specific place each category lives (a drawer, a labeled folder, a digital folder), and a recurring habit, on a specific day each month, for reviewing and updating the whole system.
materials: a blank document-system planning template provided on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Before designing the system, distinguish it from a single-event folder.

prompts.text: In your own words, explain the difference between organizing paperwork for one single event (like one doctor visit) and building an ongoing system the persona keeps running every month.

tasks.directions: Name the ongoing document categories the system will track and where each one lives.

prompts.text: I named at least four ongoing document categories relevant to independent living (for example, housing, income and budget, health, identification).
I assigned a specific storage location to every category, not a vague 'somewhere safe.'

tasks.directions: Design the recurring monthly review habit that keeps the whole system from going stale.

prompts.text: Pick a specific day each month for the persona's document review (for example, the first Sunday), and write a short checklist of exactly what the persona does during that review - which categories get checked, what happens to anything outdated or no longer needed, and how a new document gets filed into the correct category the same week it arrives rather than piling up.

tasks.directions: Evaluate whether the system would actually hold up over a full year.

prompts.text: Which document category is most likely to be forgotten during a busy month, and what about your system's design would catch that before it becomes a problem?

remediation: If a learner's system is really just one big 'important papers' pile with no categories or review habit, reteach by having them sort five sample document types (a lease, a pay stub, a doctor's note, an ID, a receipt) into named categories together, then build the monthly review habit around those same categories.
extension: Have the learner design what happens to the system when one category outgrows its storage location (for example, income records piling up after a year), adding a specific rule for when and how the persona archives or discards old documents.
